Metadata.title: SecureCargo — Physics-tested cargo securement
Metadata.description: Check before the trip whether a truck's cargo is well distributed and properly secured: photo, physics simulation and the smallest fix that meets the rules of Brazil, the US or the EU.

hero.title: Physics-tested cargo securement.
hero.subtitle: Simulate the trip before the truck leaves: see what slides, what tips and what to fix.
hero.photoAlt: Black-and-white photograph of cargo held down by straps on a truck.
hero.note: A sample photo goes through the whole inspection. No account needed.

steps.label: How it works
steps.title: Three steps, a few minutes, before the truck leaves.

photo.title: Photo
photo.body: Take one photo of the loaded truck, or two: from the side and from the rear corner, framed by guides drawn from our 3D truck. AI reads the cargo, the lashings and the truck; you confirm the truck and give the weight, or read it from the invoice.

result.title: Result
result.body: A physics simulation drives the load through 7 situations, from hard braking to a long mountain descent, and checks the rules of Brazil, the US or the EU.

fix.title: Fix and proof
fix.body: It shows the smallest change that makes the load safe and proves it in simulation. A new photo of the fixed load confirms it.

result.label: The result
result.title: One of three answers, in one sentence.
result.body: The result opens on the worst situation: what happens, why, and how to fix it. Below it, every rule and situation, grouped by status, each with its legal source. The same three states appear for the driver, in the manager's dashboard and on the certificate. Tap one to open the sample.

approved.load: Concrete pipes on a crane truck, after the fix
approved.sentence: Arrives intact and complies once two straps go over the pipes, beside the chains: it holds in all 7 situations and meets the rules. As photographed, with chains only, 0 of 7.

holds.sentence: It holds in all 7 situations, but a rule fails: an axle group carries more than its legal limit.

fails.sentence: It holds in 1 of 7 situations: on a long mountain descent, a stack of crates falls off the truck. With the fix, 7 of 7.

simulation.label: The simulation
simulation.title: See what happens, and why.
simulation.body: Each situation is a MuJoCo physics simulation of the truck bed: emergency braking, a sudden lane change, a sharp curve, a pothole, a speed bump, a long descent and long vibration on a dirt road. The replay shows the run on a 3D truck; its engineering view draws the forces as arrows.
simulation.caption: Pallets with one strap each, as loaded and fixed. {event}.

rules.label: The rules
rules.title: Brazil, the United States or the European Union.
rules.body: The same simulation, checked against the rules where the truck runs, in their units. Every rule that fails shows its article.

br.title: Brazil
br.body: CONTRAN Resolution 945/2022 for cargo lashing, and 882/2021 for weights per axle and dimensions.

us.title: United States
us.body: 49 CFR 393 subpart I for cargo securement, and the federal weight limits and bridge formula of 23 CFR 658.

eu.title: European Union
eu.body: Directive 2014/47/EU Annex III with EN 12195-1 and EN 12642, and the weights and dimensions of Directive 96/53/EC.

emergency-braking.as_loaded: As loaded, the pallets slide forward and one hits the headboard.
emergency-braking.fixed: With diagonal straps at the corners too, the load does not move.

weigh-station.as_loaded: The load holds, but the rear axle is over the legal limit.
weigh-station.fixed: With the machine moved forward, both axles are within the limit.

rope-lashing.as_loaded: Tied with rope, the stacks slide sideways in the lane change.
rope-lashing.fixed: With ratchet straps over them and diagonal straps, the stacks do not move.

sharp-curve.as_loaded: Standing free, the cabinets tip over and fall off the truck.
sharp-curve.fixed: Under a strap each and with diagonal straps, the cabinets stay upright.

steel-coil.as_loaded: As loaded, the coil rolls forward into the headboard.
steel-coil.fixed: In a cradle, chained through the eye, the coil does not move.

box-truck.as_loaded: The loose cartons slide the length of the box and slam into the front wall.
box-truck.fixed: Stacked against the front wall with a load bar behind, the cartons stay put.

dirt-road.as_loaded: The vibration loosens the straps, and the pallets slide when the truck brakes.
dirt-road.fixed: With diagonal straps at the corners, the pallets do not move.

anti-slip-mat.as_loaded: On the bare floor, the plastic pallets slide forward under braking.
anti-slip-mat.fixed: On anti-slip mats, the same two straps hold them; diagonal straps keep the load within the rules.

full-trip.as_loaded: Unlashed, the crates creep forward on the descent and slide on at the final stop.
full-trip.fixed: With four diagonal straps per crate, nothing moves for the whole trip.

curtain-sider.as_loaded: With nothing over them, the drums slide across the deck in the curve: the curtain does not hold them.
curtain-sider.fixed: In one row, under a strap and diagonal straps, the drums stay where they stand.

potholed-road.as_loaded: The pothole throws the loose pipes up; they roll and slide into the headboard.
potholed-road.fixed: Chained forward and back on both sides, the pipes stay put.

overloaded-strap.as_loaded: The coil rolls against its two straps and pulls them past their rated capacity.
overloaded-strap.fixed: In a cradle the coil cannot roll; the two straps just keep it in place.

us-steel-coils.as_loaded: The coils roll against their straps: 49 CFR 393.120 asks for a cradle and chains through the eye.
us-steel-coils.fixed: In cradles, chained through the eye forward and back, the coils hold and the load complies.

eu-curtain-pallets.as_loaded: The pallets slide through the curtain and off the trailer: a code L curtain holds nothing, a dangerous deficiency at a roadside check.
eu-curtain-pallets.fixed: On anti-slip mats, with two straps over each pallet, they hold in the curve and the load complies with Annex III.

emergency-braking.as_loaded: Three pallets with one strap each. One strap does not press a pallet down hard enough for friction to hold it in an emergency stop.
emergency-braking.fixed: The same pallets, one strap over each and four diagonal straps from its corners to the rails, forward and back. CONTRAN Resolution 945/2022 asks for diagonal devices on a flatbed, whose panels are not a containment.

weigh-station.as_loaded: An 8 t machine chained down near the back of the bed. Nothing moves over the speed bump, but most of its weight lands on the rear axle and the steering axle is left light.
weigh-station.fixed: The same machine moved forward, over the middle of the wheelbase. Its weight is shared between the two axles.

rope-lashing.as_loaded: Stacks on plastic pallets, each tied with two ropes. Rope stretches and cannot be tightened like a ratchet strap, and Brazilian rules do not allow it as cargo lashing.
rope-lashing.fixed: Two ratchet straps over each stack in place of the ropes, and four diagonal straps from its corners to the rails.

sharp-curve.as_loaded: Two tall cabinets with no lashing. The curve pushes them sideways harder than their narrow base can resist.
sharp-curve.fixed: A strap over each cabinet presses it down, and four diagonal straps at its corners keep it from tipping and hold it forward and back, since it stands above the headboard (CONTRAN 945/2022, Art. 8).

steel-coil.as_loaded: A 10 t coil lying across the bed, "eye to the side", with nothing in front of it. A cylinder needs no friction to move: braking makes it roll.
steel-coil.fixed: The same coil in a cradle: a 20 cm chock on each side. It would take 0.88 g of braking to roll it over a chock; the truck can brake at 0.64 g on a wet road. Four chains through the eye, forward and back, are its lashing.

box-truck.as_loaded: Six cartons left at the back of the box with nothing around them. Cardboard on plywood has a friction factor of only 0.3, and in fog the driver brakes late and hard.
box-truck.fixed: The same cartons stacked in two layers against the front wall, with a load bar behind them. The wall takes what friction cannot, well within its rating.

dirt-road.as_loaded: Pallets of sacks under three straps each. That is enough on this dusty deck while the straps are tight, but hours of vibration halve their tension before the final stop.
dirt-road.fixed: Four diagonal straps from the corners of each pallet to the bed. They hold by their strength, not by their tension, so loosening does not matter.

anti-slip-mat.as_loaded: Three stacks on plastic pallets, two straps each, on the plywood floor. Plastic on plywood has a friction factor of 0.2, so the straps would have to press very hard.
anti-slip-mat.fixed: The same pallets and straps, on rubber anti-slip mats with a friction factor of 0.6, plus four diagonal straps per pallet, which CONTRAN Resolution 945/2022 asks for on a flatbed.

full-trip.as_loaded: Six 1.5 t crates on a semi-trailer, left without lashings because they are heavy. Weight does not help: friction grows with it, and so does inertia.
full-trip.fixed: Four diagonal straps on each crate, forward and back on both sides. They hold through the descent, the speed bump and the emergency stop.

curtain-sider.as_loaded: Eight 200-litre drums against one side of a light curtain-sider, unlashed. A curtain-sider's curtain is weather protection: in a code L body it counts for 0 % of the payload as a restraint.
curtain-sider.fixed: The same drums in one row down the middle of the deck, 10 cm behind the headboard, each under one strap and with four diagonal straps to the rails. Side by side, a drum's strap would have to cross its neighbour.

potholed-road.as_loaded: Three 6 m steel pipes lying loose on a muddy deck (friction capped at 0.2). The pothole lifts them, and round pipes roll once they move.
potholed-road.fixed: Four chains on each pipe, forward and backward on both sides: they hold by their strength, whatever the deck.

overloaded-strap.as_loaded: A 10 t coil lying across a semi-trailer under two top-over straps. Nothing in front of it stops the roll, so the straps take it.
overloaded-strap.fixed: Two 20 cm chocks hold the coil in a cradle; the same two straps hold it down.

us-steel-coils.as_loaded: Two 19,800 lb coils lying across a 48 ft flatbed, each under two straps over the top. Nothing stops them rolling.
us-steel-coils.fixed: Each coil sits in a cradle and is chained through its eye with four chains, two forward and two back.

eu-curtain-pallets.as_loaded: Eleven 700 kg pallets against the headboard of a 13.6 m code L curtain-sider, with no lashing. Friction alone (μ 0.45) is less than the 0.5 g the EU rules ask for sideways.
eu-curtain-pallets.fixed: Anti-slip mats (μ 0.6) and two straps over each pallet hold more than half its weight sideways and 0.8 of it forward with the headboard (EN 12195-1).

devices_allowed.pass: Allowed devices: straps, chains, blocking or mats.
devices_allowed.fail: Ropes are used to lash the cargo.
devices_allowed.explain: Ropes stretch and break: the rule allows them only to hold a tarp.
devices_allowed.fix: Replace each rope with a ratchet strap or a chain.

safety_factor.pass: The straps are strong enough for the weight.
safety_factor.fail: The straps are too weak for the weight.
safety_factor.na: Held by blocking or the body's walls: not assessed.
safety_factor.explain: Together, the straps' rated capacity must be at least twice the cargo's weight. Straps made to ABNT NBR 15883-2 show their rated capacity (LC) on the label.
safety_factor.fix: Add straps, or use stronger ones (check the LC on the label).

four_terminals.pass: Each unit is lashed at 4 points or more.
four_terminals.fail: A unit has fewer than 4 lashing points.
four_terminals.explain: On an open body, every separate unit needs at least 4 strap ends hooked to the truck.
four_terminals.fix: Put two straps over each unit (each one has two ends).

anchoring.pass: Straps are hooked to the metal frame.
anchoring.fail: Straps are hooked to the wooden floor.
anchoring.explain: A wooden floor or side board can tear out; the metal frame holds.
anchoring.fix: Hook every strap to the lashing points on the metal frame.

diagonals_for_gaps.pass: No room to slide along the truck.
diagonals_for_gaps.fail: The load has room to slide forward or back.
diagonals_for_gaps.explain: Cargo that does not fill the body's length needs diagonal straps against moving forward and back.
diagonals_for_gaps.fix: Push the load against the headboard, or add diagonal straps.

above_headboard.pass: Nothing above the headboard can slide over it.
above_headboard.fail: Cargo above the headboard could slide over it.
above_headboard.na: The front wall is full height.
above_headboard.confirm: The load may stand above the headboard: confirm its height.
above_headboard.explain: If cargo stands taller than the headboard, nothing stops it going over the cab.
above_headboard.fix: Hold it with diagonal straps or blocking, or lower it below the headboard.

diagonals_open_body.pass: Diagonals or blocking hold every unit forward and back.
diagonals_open_body.fail: No diagonal lashings on an open body.
diagonals_open_body.na: The body's front and rear walls hold the load.
diagonals_open_body.explain: An open body or a platform has no panels that hold cargo, so every unit needs diagonal straps or chains against moving forward and back, even with no gap.
diagonals_open_body.fix: Add diagonal straps or chains to each unit, or block it front and back.

headboard_strength.pass: The headboard is strong enough for the cargo against it.
headboard_strength.fail: The headboard is too weak for the cargo against it.
headboard_strength.na: No cargo uses the headboard as a stop.
headboard_strength.confirm: The cargo leans on the headboard: confirm it is strong enough to stop it.
headboard_strength.explain: A headboard used as a stop must be strong enough for the cargo against it. The law gives no number; braking can push with most of the cargo's weight.
headboard_strength.fix: Use a rated headboard, or hold the cargo with diagonal straps or blocking.

en.straps: {unit}: {installed, plural, =0 {no straps} one {# strap} other {# straps}}; the standard asks for {required}.
en.fails: {unit}: does not meet the NBR 15883-1 / EN 12195-1 calculation.
en.notAssessed: {unit}: not assessed by the NBR 15883-1 / EN 12195-1 calculation here.
en.explain: How many straps hold a unit by friction, by the calculation of ABNT NBR 15883-1, Brazil's lashing standard. It is based on the European EN 12195-1, whose method and numbers we use. A technical standard, not law: CONTRAN 945 is what is enforced.
en.fix: Add straps until each unit has as many as the standard asks for.

weight.axle: {axle, select, front {Front axle} steer {Steer axle} tractor {Tractor drive axles} trailer {Trailer axles} other {Rear axle}}: {load} of {limit} allowed
weight.axleExplain: Scales fine above {tolerance} (the 12.5 % tolerance), but loading must respect the limit itself.
weight.axleFix: Move the load forward or back to share it between the axles, or take some off.
weight.payloadExplain: No truck may carry more than its maker allows (the payload on the door sticker).
weight.payloadFix: Use a bigger truck or split the load.
weight.gross: Truck and cargo {gross}; the limit is {limit}
weight.grossExplain: A rigid truck may weigh 29 t with its cargo; a tractor and semi-trailer 45 t, or 54.5 t with a triple axle and more than 16 m.
weight.grossFix: Take some of the load off.
weight.lateralOk: The weight is centred side to side.
weight.lateral: The weight sits {offset} off centre, to one side.
weight.lateral_balanceExplain: Weight on one side leans the truck in curves and loads one row of tyres.
weight.lateral_balanceFix: Move heavy units towards the middle of the deck.
weight.frontOk: Enough weight stays on the front axle to steer.
weight.front: Only {share} of the weight is on the front axle.
weight.front_axle_shareExplain: With too little weight up front, the truck steers and brakes worse.
weight.front_axle_shareFix: Move heavy units forward, towards the cab.
weight.us_axle: {axle, select, steer {Steer axle} tractor {Drive axles} trailer {Trailer axles} front {Front axle} other {Rear axle}}: {load} of {limit} allowed
weight.us_axleExplain: Federal limit: 20,000 lb on one axle, 34,000 lb on a tandem. The limits include every tolerance.
weight.us_axleFix: Move the load forward or back to share it between the axles, or take some off.
weight.us_gross: Truck and cargo {gross}; the limit is {limit}
weight.us_grossExplain: No vehicle may weigh more than 80,000 lb on the Interstate System.
weight.us_grossFix: Take some of the load off.
weight.bridgeExplain: The bridge formula limits every group of axles by how many they are and how far apart: W = 500 (LN/(N−1) + 12N + 36).
weight.bridgeFix: Spread the weight over more axles or a longer wheelbase, or carry less.
weight.payloadUsExplain: Stay within the payload on the truck's GVWR label.
weight.eu_axle: {axle, select, steer {Steer axle} drive {Driving axle} tractor {Tractor's axles} trailer {Trailer's axles} front {Front axle} other {Rear axle}}: {load} of {limit} allowed
weight.eu_axleExplain: EU limit for a single axle that does not drive: 10 t.
weight.eu_drivingExplain: EU limit for a driving axle: 11.5 t.
weight.eu_groupExplain: EU limit for a group of axles {spread} apart (Directive 96/53/EC Annex I).
weight.eu_gross: Truck and cargo {gross}; the limit is {limit}
weight.eu_grossExplain: International traffic: 18 t for two axles, 26 t for three, 40 t for an articulated vehicle.
weight.eu_grossFix: Take some of the load off.
weight.eu_driving_share: Weight on the driving axle: {share} of the total
weight.eu_driving_shareExplain: In international traffic the driving axle carries at least 25 % of the total weight, for grip.
weight.eu_driving_shareFix: Move the load forward, over the driving axle.
weight.payloadEuExplain: Stay within the weights on the manufacturer's plate.
weight.axleGrossOnly: A vehicle of this size ({regulatory} legal total) is weighed on its total only; the axles are fined only when the total is over its 5 % tolerance. The axle limit is still the law.

checks.physicsExplain: Simulated with the physics engine: the truck, this load and its straps, at {speed}.
checks.physicsFix: See “How to make it safe” below.

anti_slip_mat.explain: A rubber mat triples the grip between the cargo and the deck, so the straps need to hold less.
anti_slip_mat.fix: Put anti-slip mats under the units.

edge_protectors.advice: Use edge protectors under the straps.
edge_protectors.explain: Where a strap crosses cartons or sacks it cuts in and loses tension; a corner protector spreads the force.
edge_protectors.fix: Put a corner protector under each strap on the cargo's edges.

protection.headboardConfirm: Headboard height to confirm: we used {height}; the load reaches {top}.
protection.headboardExplain: The headboard (the wall behind the cab) stops the load in hard braking only up to its height.
protection.headboardExplainUs: The headboard stops the load in hard braking only up to its height; against cargo it must reach 4 ft or the cargo's height.

dimensions.heightExplain: Truck and load together may not be taller than 4.40 m.
dimensions.heightFix: Lower the load or load less height.

aggregate_wll.pass: The tiedowns' working load limits add up to at least half the weight.
aggregate_wll.fail: The tiedowns' working load limits add up to less than half the weight.
aggregate_wll.na: The van's walls hold the load: no tiedowns to count.
aggregate_wll.values: Worst article: {aggregate} of {required} needed · {indirect} over the top, {direct} direct.
aggregate_wll.explain: A tiedown over the top, side to side, counts its full WLL; one from the truck to the cargo (direct) counts half.
aggregate_wll.fix: Add tiedowns over the top, or use ones with a higher WLL (on the label).

min_tiedowns.pass: Enough tiedowns for each article's length and weight.
min_tiedowns.fail: Too few tiedowns for an article's length and weight.
min_tiedowns.values: {installed} installed, {required} required{blocked, select, yes { (blocked in front)} other {}}.
min_tiedowns.explain: Up to 5 ft and 1,100 lb: 1; up to 10 ft: 2; then one more for every 10 ft. Blocked in front: one per 10 ft.
min_tiedowns.fix: Add tiedowns, or push the cargo against the headboard so it is blocked in front.

front_end_structure.pass: The headboard is tall and strong enough for the cargo against it.
front_end_structure.fail: The headboard is too low or too weak for the cargo against it.
front_end_structure.confirm: Confirm the headboard: it must hold {demand} forward and reach {height}.
front_end_structure.values: Simulated wall load: {load} at worst; the 393.114(c) minimum is {minimum}{within, select, yes { (within it)} other { (above it)}}{declared, select, none {.} other {; declared rating {declared}.}}
front_end_structure.ratingLabel: Declared rating ({unit}), from the headboard's plate
front_end_structure.explain: Against the cargo it blocks, the headboard must reach 4 ft (or the cargo's height) and hold half the cargo's weight (0.4 if 6 ft or taller).
front_end_structure.fix: Use a taller or rated headboard, or hold the cargo with tiedowns instead.

van_contained.pass: Every article touches the front wall or the cargo ahead.
van_contained.fail: Cargo has room to move inside the van.
van_contained.explain: Cargo in a van with walls of adequate strength must be in contact with, or close to, a wall or other cargo.
van_contained.fix: Close the gaps, or add blocking, bracing or load bars.

rolling_articles.pass: Everything that could roll is chocked or cradled.
rolling_articles.na: Nothing on the deck is likely to roll.
rolling_articles.explain: Pipes, coils and other round cargo need chocks, wedges or a cradle that cannot come loose.
rolling_articles.fix: Chock or cradle the round cargo.

metal_coils.pass: Every coil is cradled and chained through the eye, forward and back.
metal_coils.fail: A coil lacks a cradle or chains through its eye.
metal_coils.na: No metal coils of 5,000 lb or more.
metal_coils.explain: A coil of 5,000 lb or more with its eye crosswise needs a cradle that lifts it off the deck and tiedowns through the eye against forward and rearward motion; straps over the top are not enough.
metal_coils.fix: Put each coil in a cradle and chain it through the eye, forward and back.

machinery.pass: Each machine has at least four tiedowns at its front and rear.
machinery.fail: A machine has fewer than four tiedowns at its front and rear.
machinery.na: No machinery of 10,000 lb or more.
machinery.explain: Machinery of 10,000 lb or more on wheels or tracks needs at least four tiedowns, close to its front and rear.
machinery.fix: Chain the machine at four points, two at the front and two at the rear.

anchor_points.pass: Tiedowns are hooked to the truck's anchor points.
anchor_points.fail: Tiedowns are hooked to the wooden floor or rails.
anchor_points.explain: Anchor points must be strong enough for the load; a wooden floor or rail is not one.
anchor_points.fix: Hook every tiedown to a rated anchor point on the frame.

rope_tiedowns.confirm: Ropes are allowed: confirm they have no knots and can be re-tightened.
rope_tiedowns.explain: A tiedown may not contain knots, and the driver must be able to tighten it on the road. Unmarked rope counts with a low working load limit.
rope_tiedowns.fix: Use ratchet straps, or ropes without knots on a tensioner.

wll_criterion.pass: At normal hard braking, no tiedown goes past its working load limit.
wll_criterion.fail: At normal hard braking a tiedown would go past its working load limit.
wll_criterion.na: The van's walls hold the load.
wll_criterion.explain: Braking at 0.435 g, 0.5 g backwards or 0.25 g sideways must not load any tiedown past its WLL (on the label). The harder 0.8 g case only has to stay below the breaking strength.
wll_criterion.fix: Add tiedowns, use ones with a higher WLL, or block the cargo.

themesEu.securing: How it is secured · EU Directive 2014/47 Annex III

checks.physicsArticleEu: MuJoCo simulation · Annex III loads (0.8 g forward, 0.5 g back and sideways)

values.friction: Friction alone (μ {mu}) is enough in this direction.
values.walls: Code {code}: headboard {front}, side walls {side}, rear wall {rear}
values.straps: Straps: LC {lc} · STF {stf} (as on the label)

eu_forward.pass: Held forward in hard braking ({g} g).
eu_forward.fail: Not held forward in hard braking ({g} g).
eu_forward.confirm: Held forward only if the headboard is rated for it: confirm its EN 12642 code.
eu_forward.explain: EU rules: the securing must hold 0.8 times the cargo's weight forward. Friction, straps, chains and a wall in contact add up (EN 12195-1).
eu_forward.fix: Push the load against the headboard, add straps over it or diagonals in front.

eu_sideways.pass: Held sideways in curves and lane changes ({g} g).
eu_sideways.fail: Not held sideways in curves and lane changes ({g} g).
eu_sideways.confirm: Held sideways only if the walls are rated for it.
eu_sideways.explain: The securing must hold half the cargo's weight sideways. A code L curtain holds nothing; an XL curtain or a box wall holds when the load touches it (15 cm of gap at most).
eu_sideways.fix: Add straps over the load, close the gaps across the width, or use a code XL body.

eu_rearward.fail: Not held towards the rear ({g} g).
eu_rearward.confirm: Held towards the rear only if the rear wall is rated for it.
eu_rearward.explain: The securing must hold half the cargo's weight towards the rear (pulling away, going uphill).
eu_rearward.fix: Add straps over the load or diagonals behind it, or close the load up to the rear doors.

eu_tipping.pass: Units that could tip over are held upright.
eu_tipping.fail: A unit that could tip over is not held upright.
eu_tipping.confirm: Confirm the tall units are held upright.
eu_tipping.na: Every unit is stable on its own.
eu_tipping.explain: Annex III asks the securing to prevent tilting and tipping. A unit taller than its base is wide tips before it slides.
eu_tipping.fix: Add straps over the top, diagonals attached high, or block it against a wall as tall as its centre.

eu_body_strength.pass: The walls the load leans on are counted at their EN 12642 rating.
eu_body_strength.fail: The curtains of a code L curtain-sider hold no cargo.
eu_body_strength.confirm: The walls are taken as code L: check the code on the body's plate.
eu_body_strength.na: A flatbed: no body walls are counted.
eu_body_strength.explain: EN 12642 rates the body: code L headboard 40 % of the payload (5,000 daN at most), code XL 50 %; code XL walls and curtains 40 %. A code L curtain is weather protection only.
eu_body_strength.fix: Lash the load as if there were no curtains, or load it in a code XL body.

eu_headboard_height.pass: The headboard is as tall as the cargo leaning on it.
eu_headboard_height.fail: The cargo leaning on the headboard is taller than it.
eu_headboard_height.confirm: Confirm the headboard's height: the cargo leans on it.
eu_headboard_height.na: No cargo leans on a flatbed's headboard.
eu_headboard_height.explain: A front wall too low for the cargo it blocks is a dangerous deficiency (Annex III, Table 1 item 10.1.2).
eu_headboard_height.fix: Lower the load, or lash it so it does not rely on the headboard.

eu_devices.pass: Rated straps or chains, marked with their LC and STF.
eu_devices.fail: Ropes are used as lashings: they are not rated devices.
eu_devices.confirm: Check the labels of the lashings.
eu_devices.explain: EU lashings follow EN 12195-2 (straps), -3 (chains) and -4 (wire ropes) and carry a label with their lashing capacity (LC) and standard tension (STF) in daN.
eu_devices.fix: Replace the ropes with labelled ratchet straps.

eu_lashing_points.pass: The lashing points hold what the lashings pull.
eu_lashing_points.fail: The lashing points are weaker than the lashings on them.
eu_lashing_points.explain: EN 12640: each lashing point holds 800 daN on a vehicle up to 7.5 t, 1,000 daN up to 12 t and 2,000 daN above. A chain can pull more than its point holds.
eu_lashing_points.fix: Use more lashing points per unit, or rated points (4,000 daN), and hook lashings to the frame, not the wooden floor.
